headline: UK Energy Regulator Ofgem Raises Typical Household Bills by 26% in January
summary: Regulator Ofgem announced that typical annual gas and electricity bills in Great Britain will rise by 26% in January, pushing annual bills over £2,000.
why: Energy price caps set by Ofgem directly impact household disposable incomes and utility costs across the UK, influencing consumer spending and broader inflation metrics.

impacts.name: FTSE 100
impacts.why: Higher energy bills weigh on consumer discretionary stocks and broader market sentiment.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Rising utility costs create immediate pressures on consumer budgets and corporate sentiment, prompting a broad retreat in UK equities.
